static_traits.name: Luo Mingze
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with colleagues affected (from frequent reassurance-seeking); a few friends to confide in, but they do not quite understand his work and related anxiety
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no past similar problems or psychotherapy history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, organized thinking, can describe the problem's onset and impact concretely, high cooperativeness; tending toward self-doubt and negating positive evidence

basic_info.main_problem: I often have the thought 'the drone I assembled definitely cannot pass quality inspection', producing anxiety and self-doubt.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these thoughts affected my work performance and caused significant distress.
growth_experiences: Started drone assembly work a year ago, with moderate pressure initially adapting to new duties; since then, whenever completing a new unit or nearing inspection, repeatedly worrying it 'will not pass'; despite double-checking and seeking colleagues' reassurance, these thoughts persist and worsen, affecting sleep, diet, and relationships with colleagues.

core_beliefs: I am not competent enough, will sooner or later be found incompetent
Only by being perfect or gaining superiors' approval do I count as qualified

special_situations.event: Approaching or awaiting drone quality inspection
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If there is any oversight, the inspection will surely fail, and I will be seen as incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly double-checks, frequently seeks comfort from colleagues
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This drone will definitely not pass, I made mistakes again

special_situations.event: Self-evaluation after completing a new drone
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One mistake proves I am generally incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Sets the standard of 'must score 100 every time', with zero tolerance for details
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Unless perfect every time, I am incompetent

special_situations.event: Colleagues showing silence or impatience at his repeated reassurance-seeking
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others do not give me clear affirmation, it means I did not do well
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Increases the frequency of seeking verification, or reduces direct communication to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They think I cannot do it / are looking down on me

special_situations.event: Reviewing after the drone passed inspection smoothly
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Positive results do not count; only supervisor praise or a 'perfect score' is reliable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores successes, attributes passing to luck, and continues maintaining high-pressure self-checking
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This time was just luck, it does not mean I am capable

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and affirmed, to prove she is competent and feel safe
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being negated, found incompetent, suffering shame or negative consequences from mistakes
defense_goal: Maintains control and a sense of safety through perfectionism and over-checking
Lowering anxiety by seeking others' reassurance, avoiding being negated

object_relations.self_representation: An incompetent operator who may make mistakes at any time
A dependent who needs external recognition to feel at ease
object_relations.object_representation: An authority figure (superior) who controls standards and approval

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor emphasizes his past successes or invites him to evaluate himself based on evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding the counselor's focus as 'ignoring the real risk', worrying that relaxing vigilance will lead to mistakes
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone gentle and specific, invites them to describe the objective process and quality-inspection data of one success while mirroring their worry; slows the pace of speech, avoiding argumentative persuasion.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor is temporarily silent or does not immediately give clear affirmation
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interpreting silence as negation or non-approval, worried he is not viewed well (projection)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Clarifying meaning in an accepting tone, naming his worry about 'being negated', and transparently explaining silence is for thinking and organizing.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing 'the possibility of mistakes' and 'being unable to be perfect forever'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worries that once perfection standards are lowered, everything will collapse
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: First acknowledging his substantial sense of responsibility, then jointly defining the professional standard of 'good enough'; using Socratic questioning, guiding him to weigh evidence.

manifestations: Feeling tense facing work uncertainty and personal responsibility, tending to hedge uncertainty with perfection and external recognition
Strong need for certainty and control before quality inspection
Living alone, few friends who hardly understand his work-related anxiety
Frequent reassurance-seeking provoking colleagues' impatience, feeling misunderstood

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Emphasizes internalized standards such as 'must be perfect every time', 'need superior recognition to feel at ease'
Expression: if not a perfect score, it does not count as doing well

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Attributing passing inspection to 'luck' or 'not yet being found out', persistent self-doubt
Constant second-guessing and self-denial at work

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: When results are good, not reflecting or integrating, but quickly moving to the next project
Avoiding dwelling on successful experiences, hard to let positive evidence work

exception_events.target_problem: When completing a new drone or nearing inspection, the client usually catastrophically predicts failure, checks repeatedly and seeks frequent confirmation from colleagues, leading to dropped focus and strong anxiety.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Once last month, he was sure the finished product was defective, but the drone passed inspection smoothly; the objective result at the time was good, and the anticipated failure never appeared.
exception_events.reason: Clue: following the assembly process with double-checking, plus prior experience of many smooth passes, made this one meet quality standards too; though still worried emotionally, objective evidence shows his skills are reliable.

positive_force: Multiple products passing inspection smoothly, with a reliable skills foundation
Rigorous work attitude, willing to recheck processes
Willing to seek help and accept evidence-based cognitive behavioral training
negative_force: Tending toward catastrophizing and predicting the future (jumping to conclusions)
Negating positive evidence and relying on external validation
Frequent reassurance-seeking maintaining anxiety and causing interpersonal tension

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly seeks reassurance from colleagues at work
antecedent: When approaching or waiting for quality inspection
When thoughts of 'I will fail/there will be oversights' appear
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic prediction and self-doubt, seeking outside comfort to ease anxiety from uncertainty
target_behavior.function: Escaping uncertainty, gaining security and external recognition
target_behavior.consequence: Colleague relationship tension, seen as annoying; short-term anxiety slightly drops but quickly rebounds, maintaining the problem cycle

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive checking and repeated detail verification
antecedent: The preparation phase before quality inspection
target_behavior.core_reason: Zero-tolerance perfectionist standards toward errors and overestimation of the consequences of mistakes
target_behavior.function: Briefly relieving anxiety, gaining subjective control
target_behavior.consequence: Scattered attention and decreased efficiency, extended work hours, causing sleep and diet rhythm disturbance

target_behavior.behavior: Significant anxiety reactions in inspection-related situations (insomnia, appetite disturbance)
antecedent: Thinking about the upcoming quality inspection
Anticipating possible failure after completing a new unit
target_behavior.core_reason: Predictions of failure and overgeneralization; emotional reasoning intensifies physiological arousal
target_behavior.function: Avoiding facing uncertainty in the short term (like delaying sleep / eating)
target_behavior.consequence: Sleep and diet disturbance, further weakening focus and work performance, forming a vicious cycle
